page.layout: One printed page. Main text in one column on the left. Marginal notes in a narrow column on the right, beside the upper lines. The running head is at the top, with the page number at its right. The gathering signature is at the foot.

main_text.p: & perpetua esse videntur. Verùm hìc poë-ticæ atq; nimiæ amplificationes vitandæ: præsertim apud viros bonos, doctos, prudentes, qui laudationes eas, quæ veritate excedunt; & adulationes oderunt: assu-menda quoq; ἴδια conci- liantia argu- mentaἴδια, quæ mores indicant amabiles, & ad beneuolentiam sunt confi-ciliandam accómodata: cuiusmodi sunt μειώσεις extenuationes virium atq; facultatum in referenda gratia: & εὐχαὶ vota ac precationes, vt Deus large exoluat, quod nos compensare non possumus: & [illegible, ~9 letters] praemunitiones, ne, vel adulatorie accepta beneficia amplificares; vel in peti-tione noua verecundiæ transgredi fines: aut de amici in nobis nostrisq; amandis & promouendis dubitare fide ac constan-tia videamur. Postremò etiam mouetium argumentorum est ratio habenda. Neque αὐξητικὰ [?] mo- uentia argu- mentaenim satis est laudare, celebrare, amplifi-care beneficium acceptum: verùm etiam mouere eos, ad quos scribimus, oportet: vt de sua in nos nostrófue prona propen-saque voluntate nihil remittant: & adhi-bere ea, quæ excitant: ζῆλον æmulatio-nem: ἡδονὴν voluptatem & lætitiam, φιλίαν amorem & beneuolentiam: ἐλπίδα spem animi grati & remunerationis. Ad

page.notes: The first Greek word in the upper marginal note and the Greek word after "&" in the text, which is illegible, are uncertain. The second marginal note is partly cut off at the margin, so its Greek and the word "mo-uentia" are uncertain. The page number "147" is written in an old, flourished 7. The first paragraph continues from the previous page, and the last word "Ad" carries over to the next page.
